translation_notes: the region is a 450-line nested dict (quantity_definitions) whose keys are RDF predicates and whose values are RDF terms; no triple is ever added, so the whole translation is term notation inside Python data literals

the eight imported Namespace constants become @prefix declarations; 398 QUDT/SKOS/RDFS/BRICK terms become prefixed names. Notably `{ qudt:hasDimensionVector: qudtdv:A0E0L0I0M0H0T0D1 }` works: the prefixed-name island stops at the ':' that separates a dict key from its value, so RDF predicates read naturally as dict keys -- the residual `{ex:b}` collision documented in the language reference resolves in the notation's favour here

LIMIT FOUND: outside a g{} island a prefixed name may only use the intersection of Python identifier characters and Turtle's PN_CHARS, so the 32 QUDT local names containing '-' or '.' (unit:MicroGM-PER-M3, unit:W-PER-M2-SR, qudtdv:A0E0L-3I0M0H0T-1D0, ...) cannot be written as prefixed names -- `qudtdv:A0E0L-3I0M0H0T-1D0` transpiles to `URIRef('...A0E0L')-3I0M0H0T-1D0`, i.e. a Python SyntaxError, which the mechanical draft produced. They are kept in the original UNIT[...] / QUDTDV[...] form (a full IRI island <http://qudt.org/vocab/unit/MicroGM-PER-M3> would also work but loses the abbreviation). The file therefore mixes both notations, 398 prefixed names against 32 Python fallbacks

LIMIT FOUND: the 43 plain Literal("...") / Literal(True) values also stay Python. Outside a graph island a bare "x" is a Python str, and ldpy only recognises a literal island when it carries a glued @lang or ^^datatype suffix; Brick's definitions are all plain xsd:string / xsd:boolean literals, so none of them can shed the Literal() call

the 35 occurrences of URIRef(str(BRICK).strip("#")) are left as Python: <https://brickschema.org/schema/Brick> would be the idiomatic island but it hard-codes what the original derives from the namespace, which faithfulness rule 1 forbids

g.bind("qudt", QUDT) / g.bind("qudtqk", QUDTQK) are kept verbatim, which is why the `from namespaces import ...` line is kept too: @prefix is a transpile-time declaration and provides no runtime Namespace object, so a file that both declares prefixes and binds them on a graph writes each IRI twice

context shims (identical for both sides): 'from .namespaces import ...' -> 'from namespaces import ...' and 'from .env import env' -> 'from env import env' (import lines only). namespaces.py holds the eight bindings copied from bricksrc/namespaces.py; env.py is a no-op stand-in for ontoenv (env.import_graph would download the QUDT 3.3.0 unit and quantitykind vocabularies -- the region never queries g, so the no-op is behaviour-preserving for it); brickschema/graph.py transcribes the part of brickschema.graph.Graph the region uses (prefix binding, and the add() that expands a list of (p,o) pairs into a blank node) from the BrickSchema/py-brickschema checkout

demo harness added identically to both sides: the region declares the structure but never walks it (Brick's generate_brick.py does), so a trailing stripped-down define_concept_hierarchy materialises it into DEMO_GRAPH -- 323 triples, covering every term of the structure. Renaming a single prefixed name in translated.ldpy makes the driver report the graphs non-isomorphic, so the check is discriminating
